title: Mojo Language by Modular (Now Qualcomm) is Now Open-Source Under Apache 2.0 License
summary: Modular has announced that the Mojo programming language, part of its AI-focused Modular Platform, is now fully open-source under the Apache 2.0 license. This move allows developers to extend the language, port it to new platforms, and build applications freely. Key updates include native Windows support (via collaboration with Microsoft), the general availability of Modular Cloud for AI inference, and expanded hardware support for AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, and Qualcomm AI accelerators. The MAX license has also been relaxed to encourage ecosystem contributions, and an open alliance program is in development to foster industry collaboration on heterogeneous AI compute.
key_points: Mojo 1.0 is now open-source under Apache 2.0, including the compiler and tooling, enabling unrestricted use and extension.
Native Windows support for Mojo is in development through a partnership with Microsoft’s Windows team.
Modular Cloud is publicly available, offering high-performance AI inference with support for shared and dedicated deployments.
Modular Platform now supports diverse hardware: AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, Qualcomm Cloud AI 100, and Dragonfly accelerators alongside CPUs/GPUs.
MAX license restrictions have been removed, and the platform will become source-available with an open alliance program for ecosystem collaboration.
Modular’s acquisition by Qualcomm reinforces its commitment to a vendor-neutral, heterogeneous AI software foundation.
